question: In a 200-m race, if A gives B a head start of 35 m, then A wins the race by 20 sec. Alternatively, if A gives B a head start of 55 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does A take to run 200 m?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance of the race = 200 m

Head start given to B in the first scenario = 35 m

A wins the race by 20 sec

Head start given to B in the second scenario = 55 m

The race ends in a dead heat

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

200VA=33000145×VA+20" id="MathJax-Element-28-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0"> \frac{200}{V_A} = \frac{33000}{145 \times V_A} + 20 In the first case:

A runs = 200m , B runs = (200 - 35)m = 165m

Let A take x s to run 200m then, B will take (x+20) s for 165m 

In the second case:

A runs = 200m, B runs = (200 - 55)m = 145m

Time taken by B to run 145m = time taken by A to run 200m = x s

From the first and second cases, it is clear that for (165 - 145)m = 20m extra run B takes 20 s extra time.

Thus speed of B = 20m/20s = 1m/s

Therefore, Time taken by A to run 200m = Time taken by B to run 145m = 145/1 = 145 s

**The correct answer is option 2: 145 sec.**
